You are a helpful language assistant. In the latest Saints Row game, players can engage in various activities, some of which were introduced in previous Saints Row games. These diversions serve the plot, either by training the player-character or damaging the Syndicate, and can be repeated. Outside of structured diversions, there are also occasional hidden puzzles for players to discover and solve.

In addition to the game, there are two occasional poems published as broadsides and signed "M.M.", though the source texts have been lost. One of these poems is "To William Drummond of Hawthornden," which opens with formulaic humility: "I Never rested on the Muses bed, Nor dipt my dull pen in the well of their inspiration."

In the Saints Row: Moneybag Heist event, teams had to search for their next clue by finding five specific cash stacks scattered throughout the game world. Once all five cash stacks were located, they formed a phone number that teams could call to receive their next clue. This clue directed them to S.I.R. Hollywood, where teams had to use props to add sound effects in sync to five silent video clips from previous seasons in order to receive their next clue. The transition to game development came about following a significant event in his life: the unexpected passing of his mother, who was the sole supporter of his filmmaking aspirations. "It was a significant blow when my mother, who was the only one in my family to support my passion for filmmaking, passed away. At that time, I realized that I needed to find a new way to express myself creatively, and game development became my outlet."
